import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Filter to expression and copy number features
    expr_ids = [fid for fid, typ in zip(feats.ids, feats.types) if typ in ('expression', 'copy_number')]
    
    # Compute correlation matrix
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in expr_ids]]
    corr = np.corrcoef(X.T)
    
    # Find highly correlated pairs
    high_corr_pairs = []
    for i in range(len(expr_ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(expr_ids)):
            if abs(corr[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                high_corr_pairs.append((expr_ids[i], expr_ids[j]))
    
    # If no strong correlations, use top features by t-statistic
    if not high_corr_pairs:
        t_stats = [stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                  feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)])[0] 
                   for fid in expr_ids]
        sorted_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(t_stats))[::-1][:min(4, len(expr_ids))]
        drivers = tuple([expr_ids[i] for i in sorted_indices])
        return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=drivers, products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Cluster features by correlation
    all_features = list(set([f for pair in high_corr_pairs for f in pair]))
    if len(all_features) < 2:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
        
    # Simple approach: take top 4 features by t-statistic from correlated group
    t_stats = [stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                              feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)])[0] 
               for fid in all_features]
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(np.abs(t_stats))[::-1][:min(4, len(all_features))]
    drivers = tuple([all_features[i] for i in sorted_indices])
    
    # Use all correlated features for columns but limit to 8 to reduce complexity
    module_features = all_features[:8] if len(all_features) > 8 else all_features
    
    # Simple loading: equal weights for simplicity
    loadings = {fid: 1.0 for fid in module_features}
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=tuple(module_features), products=(), loadings=loadings)
